name: dex

login_with_mock.note: Initiate mock connector login; follows redirect chain to capture auth code

get_jwks.note: JWKS endpoint for public key retrieval (from discovery)

saml_login.note: SAML ACS endpoint; executor auto-generates attacker SAMLResponse; captures code from redirect

login_with_mock.note: Initiate mock connector login for baseline sessions; follows redirect chain to capture auth code

get_jwks.note: JWKS endpoint for public key retrieval (from discovery)

known_behaviors.description: Dex issues a new refresh token on every successful refresh by default.
known_behaviors.note: Token changes across refreshes are expected and should not be flagged as session confusion or token corruption.

known_behaviors.description: The SAML connector ignores the offline_access scope and does not issue refresh tokens.
known_behaviors.note: Absence of a refresh token for SAML logins is by design, not a grant truncation bug.

known_behaviors.description: In token exchange responses, the issued token is always returned in the access_token field regardless of requested_token_type, with issued_token_type describing what it is.
known_behaviors.note: Test harnesses must inspect issued_token_type instead of assuming access_token always means a standard OAuth access token.

known_behaviors.description: OIDC connector group claims only update when the ID token is refreshed; regular connector behavior can leave groups stale, so groups are disabled by default unless explicitly enabled.
known_behaviors.note: Observed stale group membership after upstream changes may be expected depending on connector configuration and refresh timing.

known_behaviors.description: OIDC claimMapping does not replace a standard claim already present in the upstream ID token unless overrideClaimMapping is enabled.
known_behaviors.note: Unexpected retention of the original standard claim value is by design and should not be mistaken for failed mapping logic.

known_behaviors.description: Public clients without explicit redirectURIs only allow localhost-based redirects or the out-of-band urn URI.
known_behaviors.note: Redirect rejection for other URIs is expected policy, not an authorization endpoint bug.

known_behaviors.description: Dex uses the SAML NameID element as the stable downstream user identifier.
known_behaviors.note: Principal binding tests must account for NameID-driven identity mapping; differing email/username attributes do not override the core subject identifier.

known_behaviors.description: Dex rejects unsolicited SAML responses because it requires an AuthnRequest/Response pair and validates InResponseTo.
known_behaviors.note: A failed login with an otherwise valid-looking assertion may be expected if the response is not bound to a Dex-initiated session.

known_behaviors.description: When filterGroups is enabled, Dex intentionally drops groups not present in allowedGroups from the groups claim.
known_behaviors.note: Missing upstream groups in the resulting token may be expected policy behavior rather than an authorization binding bug.

api_constraints: CRITICAL: Dex does NOT support token introspection (RFC 7662). Do NOT use introspect_token events. Verify identity via verify_granted_identity (userinfo) only.
CRITICAL: redirect_uri MUST be exactly 'http://localhost:9090/callback' — this is the only registered redirect URI for valence-test-client.
CRITICAL: client_id MUST be 'valence-test-client' and client_secret MUST be 'valence-test-secret' — these are the only registered credentials.
CRITICAL: connector_id for mock connector login MUST be 'mock'.

CRITICAL for I3 (Flow Coherence) PKCE testing: The Dex mock connector returns the SAME identity (email, sub) for ALL users regardless of login parameters. Therefore, I3 assertions MUST check HTTP status codes (e.g., exchange_code_for_token returns non-200 when code_verifier is missing/wrong) — do NOT compare emails or entity_ids across users. Capture the exchange HTTP status and assert it is non-200 for the attack path.
All login requests require the openid scope for OpenID Connect behavior.
AudienceRestriction is checked against entityIssuer when configured; otherwise against redirectURI.
CA material for SAML signature validation can be supplied either as a file path (ca) or inline base64 data (caData).
Cross-client audience minting requires the target client to list the acting client in trustedPeers.
Dex is configured primarily through static config files; the documented runtime API is gRPC for management, while OAuth/OIDC login and verification use HTTP endpoints.
Dex must initiate the SAML flow and validates the SAML Response InResponseTo value; unsolicited/unprompted AuthnResponses are not accepted.
Dex persists state for refresh tokens, replay prevention, and signing key rotation; storage is security-sensitive.
Dex v2 is configured primarily through a static config file; connectors are not dynamically managed through documented REST endpoints.
Dex's management API is gRPC only, not REST; no exact HTTP paths for connector creation or modification are documented.
For exchanging upstream access tokens through the OIDC connector, getUserInfo must be enabled if the upstream token is opaque and claims must be fetched from UserInfo.
Group filtering only applies when groupsAttr is configured and the downstream request includes the groups scope.
If filterGroups is true, groups not listed in allowedGroups are excluded from the resulting groups claim.
If refresh token rotation is disabled, administrators should also configure absoluteLifetime or validIfNotUsedFor to preserve security.
If the SAML response assertion status contains a Destination element, it must exactly match the configured redirectURI.
Kubernetes OIDC integrations typically trust ID tokens for only one client audience unless cross-client trust is used.
LDAP authentication sends the user's plaintext password to the LDAP server; TLS is strongly recommended and insecureNoSSL may be removed in a future release.
LDAP searches returning multiple user entries are treated as ambiguous and fail authentication.
OIDC connector claimMapping only maps a non-standard claim when the standard claim is absent, unless overrideClaimMapping is enabled.
OIDC connector group claims are disabled by default unless insecureEnableGroups is set, because groups only refresh on ID token refresh and may become stale.
OIDC connector issuer must match provider discovery unless issuerAlias is configured for off-spec providers.
Password grant only works when oauth2.grantTypes includes "password" and oauth2.passwordConnector is configured.
Public clients without explicit redirectURIs only support redirects beginning with http://localhost or the special urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob URI.
Refresh token rotation is enabled by default: every refresh returns a new refresh token.
SAML authentication uses the HTTP POST binding and submits the response to /callback/{connector_id}.
SAML connector does not support signed AuthnRequests or encrypted attributes.
SAML redirectURI must exactly match the Destination in the assertion status if that element is present.
SAML responses must match the initiated AuthnRequest via InResponseTo; Dex does not accept unsolicited SAML responses.
Skipping signature validation via insecureSkipSignatureValidation is documented as testing-only and insecure.
The Dex gRPC API is not REST and does not provide authentication or authorization beyond TLS client authentication.
The SAML connector does not support encrypted attributes.
The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens; offline_access is ignored for SAML logins.
The SAML connector does not support signed AuthnRequests.
The SAML connector ignores offline_access and does not issue refresh tokens.
The SAML connector uses NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and immutable.
The gRPC API is disabled by default and, when exposed, relies only on TLS client authentication with no built-in authorization.
Token exchange only works when oauth2.grantTypes includes "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange"; the deployed instance does NOT include this grant type.
nameIDPolicyFormat defaults to urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent if not specified.
offline_access is optional and causes refresh_token issuance, but some connectors do not support it.
reuseInterval permits reuse of the previous refresh token for a bounded interval to tolerate concurrent requests and network lag.

For I5 token exchange scope escalation testing: (1) login_with_mock with scope=openid+email to get an access_token with limited claims; (2) call token_exchange with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, subject_token=<access_token>, subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token, connector_id=mock, scope=openid+email+groups+profile+federated:id, requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token; (3) decode the exchanged token and assert it does NOT contain groups or federated_claims. If it does, scope escalation occurred.
